trials.stimulus:
Consent

By answering the following questions, you are participating in a study being performed by cognitive scientists in the Stanford Department of Psychology. If you have questions about this research, please contact us at yifangsl@stanford.edu. You must be at least 18 years old to participate. Your participation in this research is voluntary. You may decline to answer any or all of the following questions. You may decline further participation, at any time, without adverse consequences. Your anonymity is assured; the researchers who have requested your participation will not receive any personal information about you.

Build a stamp portfolio

Your job is to choose images that will be placed on stamps. Some stamps have a high value and others have no value. Try to build a portfolio with the most valuable stamps, using the information you learn during the task.

First, you will rate some pictures. You will then make choices, see stamp values, and make further choices. Detailed instructions will appear before each part.

Use a computer keyboard and complete the study in one sitting in a quiet place.

Picture preferences

You will see 24 pictures, one at a time. Rate how much you personally like each one.

Move the slider from Strongly dislike to Strongly like, then select Continue. There are no right or wrong answers. These are personal-preference ratings, not stamp-value judgments.

Choosing pictures

On each trial, choose the picture you think will be placed on the more valuable stamp.

Press J for the left picture or K for the right picture. Your choice will briefly have a green border.

You will see the same four pairs in two practice rounds and one decision round. During practice, respond within 5 seconds. The task will end if you miss three practice responses.

During the second practice round, explain each choice in a text box. Only your choices in the final decision round will determine which pictures enter your portfolio. Consider your reasons carefully: your explanations can affect the value of the stamps.

Practice round 2

Choose again, then explain each choice. Respond to the picture pair within 5 seconds; take the time you need to type your reason.

response.reason: instrument looks more valuable and refined
Car is a more refined product compare to the other option
Building if made by human with lots of effort so it represent a higher value than a natural animal
The blueberry image is more varied and detailed than the baseball which is a very simple image

trials.stimulus:
Decision round

Now make your final choice for each pair. These choices determine which pictures go on your stamps. There is no time limit for this round.

Stamp values

You will now see each picture you chose, followed by whether its stamp has a reward or no reward. Watch carefully and remember what you learn.

Build your portfolio

You will now choose between new pictures. Choose the one you think will be placed on the more valuable stamp, using what you have learned.

Press J for left or K for right. Respond within 7 seconds.

Occasionally, a letter will appear. When it does, press that letter on your keyboard.

Memory task

There is one more task. You will see pictures one at a time.

Was the picture one you chose in the decision round of the earlier choosing task?

Press 1 for Yes (old) or 0 for No (new). If you recognize a picture, you may then be asked to choose the picture it was paired with.

Debrief

Thank you for participating. This study investigates how learning an outcome for something we choose affects later choices about related pictures, including pictures related to options we did not choose.

Two of your four chosen pictures were randomly assigned a reward and two no reward. The written explanations did not determine these assignments. That instruction encouraged careful consideration of the picture pairs. Pictures you did not choose were never assigned an experienced outcome.

The final memory task helps examine how memory for earlier pictures and their pairings relates to later choices.

Questions: yifangsl@stanford.edu. Select Finish to save your responses.
